artworks.title: Pylades and Orestes Brought as Victims before Iphigenia
artworks.description: West's National Gallery oil sends Pylades to Tauris bound beside Orestes — the friend who shares the sacrificial altar before recognition saves them. Friendship as the third voice of Euripides' plot.

artworks.title: Orestes and Pylades (San Ildefonso Group, Prado)
artworks.description: The Prado's San Ildefonso Group — long read as Orestes and Pylades — shows two youths in sacrificial quiet. Whether Dioscuri or Oresteian companions, the marble has become the image of the friend who shares exile and blood-debt.

artworks.title: Orestes and Pylades Disputing the Sacrifice
artworks.description: Lastman paints the Taurian dilemma: which friend will die for the other. Pylades offers himself so Orestes may live — Dutch history painting as a study in classical loyalty.

artworks.title: Orestes and Pylades in Tauris (Roman fresco)
artworks.description: A Roman fresco keeps the pair before the Taurian altar — Pylades still at Orestes' shoulder as Iphigenia's recognition approaches. Ancient wall-painting of the friendship that opera later made famous.

films.title: Electra
films.description: Cacoyannis keeps Pylades as Orestes' steadfast companion — the friend who shares the road home and the blood that waits there.

music.title: Iphigénie en Tauride
music.description: Gluck's Pylades is the friend who offers to die for Orestes — the Tauris recognition trio's third voice, and one of opera's great portraits of loyalty.

music.title: Ermione
music.description: Rossini brings Pylades to Epirus at Orestes' side — still the companion, now in a court intrigue over Hermione and Andromache.
